etymologies.etymologyHTML: From logic +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: (not comparable) In agreement with the principles of logic.

quote.citation: 2020 April 6, Shanguo, “Avoiding Assertive Statements and Extreme Ways of Thinking”, in Minghui‎[1]:
quote.text: To provide convincing arguments, we need to first address the issues of concern, list the facts, and then use logical reasoning to help people have a better understanding of the issue.
I won't lie about what I didI cut her head off and threw it in a ditchWhy I only kept the body was a logical choiceI threw away the head because I hated the sound of her voice

definitions.definition: (not comparable) Of or pertaining to logic.
(computing) Relating to the conceptual model of a system rather than its physical expression

quote.citation: 1986, Noel Malcolm Morris, Computer graphics and CAD fundamentals: BBC Micro version:
quote.text: It is, of course, vital to restore the logical colours to their normal value at the end of the program […]
